ZBoard is a minimal, extensible panel for users, subscriptions, nodes and system services. This RC corrects subscription lifecycle and commerce flows, restores administration controls and improves operational statistics while preserving existing capabilities.

## Changes

- Show only operations backed by published products and saleable SKUs. Product and SKU deletion archives catalog entries while preserving historical order snapshots.
- Allow an unexpired timed subscription to change plans after its cycle traffic is exhausted, including when no reset SKU exists. Exhausted traffic has zero transferable value. Payment replaces the cycle quota with the target plan quota, retains consumed traffic and preserves expiry; it does not reset usage or append another billing period.
- Sell traffic resets through a configured one-time reset SKU and order. Pending or canceled orders do not restore quota; settlement authorization and repeat-safe fulfillment remain mandatory. A paid reset restores the subscription's base cycle quota without extending expiry or moving the next scheduled reset.
- Stop ended services immediately. Renewable subscriptions retain their instance for seven days and can recover through paid renewal during that window. Nonrenewable single-use services are cleaned up at expiry or exhaustion; historical orders retain their terminal status and final quota/usage. Late payment cannot recreate a cleaned target.
- Keep monthly subscriptions visible when current-cycle traffic is exhausted. Display available purchase operations from the actual catalog rather than offering unusable reset or renewal buttons.
- Apply administrator quota changes to the latest locked subscription, changing only submitted fields. Preserve original traffic records and reasoned before/after audit history with idempotent retries.
- Unify menu editing and input interactions, support checkbox deselection and reduce redundant SKU configuration. Preset billing periods retain custom values. Provide contextual user/order/subscription links, advanced filters, collapsed quota editing and node setup guidance.
- Add timezone-aware revenue comparisons, traffic trends and node/user rankings. Maintain hourly traffic aggregates transactionally and use bounded ledger reads for partial hours, reducing long-window reporting work. Dashboard requests load independently and cancel obsolete requests.
- Preserve plugin management, optional integrations and existing node publication capabilities. Plugin filters use shared controls and actual execution state.

## Updating

Back up the database, deployment configuration, encryption keys, plugin packages and managed rules. Use this exact RC image tag. Preserve the previous image and database backup for rollback.

This RC adds migrations `0022_catalog_archive`, `0023_subscription_lifecycle` and `0024_traffic_usage_hourly` for MySQL and SQLite. The traffic migration backfills historical records; run one instance with `-migrate-only` while other application writers are stopped, then start application instances after migration completes. Do not race MySQL DDL between instances. Preserve the existing credential encryption key.

Configure a published traffic-reset SKU, its price and the reset operation to offer paid resets. A subscription's automatic reset schedule and audited administrator adjustments remain separate from customer reset purchases. Payment providers remain optional plugins.

Local backend tests and vet, frontend tests, type checking, production builds and OpenAPI validation are checked before tagging. Browser evidence uses simulated local data. Publication does not migrate or deploy an existing installation; production database and node recovery validation remain operator steps.
